name: Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
description: Tissue systems, stomata, vascular bundles, and T.S. of dicot and monocot root, stem and leaf

cards.term: What is anatomy?
cards.definition: The study of the internal structure of plants

cards.term: How is a plant organised, from unit to organ?
cards.definition: Cells → tissues → organs

cards.term: Name the three tissue systems of a plant.
cards.definition: Epidermal, ground (fundamental), vascular (conducting)

cards.term: What makes up the epidermal tissue system?
cards.definition: Epidermal cells, stomata, and epidermal appendages (trichomes and hairs)

cards.term: Describe the epidermis.
cards.definition: Outermost layer of the primary plant body; elongated, compactly arranged, usually single-layered, parenchymatous cells with a large vacuole

cards.term: What is the cuticle, and where is it absent?
cards.definition: A waxy thick layer on the epidermis that prevents water loss; absent in roots

cards.term: What do stomata regulate?
cards.definition: Transpiration and gaseous exchange

cards.term: Shape of guard cells in most plants and in grasses?
cards.definition: Most: bean-shaped. Grasses: dumb-bell shaped.

cards.term: Which wall of a guard cell is thickened?
cards.definition: The inner wall (towards the pore); the outer wall is thin

cards.term: Why does thick inner / thin outer wall matter for opening?
cards.definition: When guard cells swell, the thin outer walls stretch more, so the cells bow outwards and the pore opens (intuition beyond NCERT)

cards.term: What are subsidiary cells?
cards.definition: Epidermal cells near the guard cells, specialised in shape and size

cards.term: What is the stomatal apparatus?
cards.definition: Stomatal aperture + guard cells + surrounding subsidiary cells

cards.term: Figure 6.1 · Stomata: (a) bean-shaped, (b) dumb-bell shaped guard cells
Root hairs vs trichomes?
cards.definition: Root hairs: unicellular outgrowths of root epidermis that absorb water. Trichomes: hairs on the stem, usually multicellular.

cards.term: Describe trichomes and their role.
cards.definition: Branched or unbranched, soft or stiff, may be secretory; they prevent water loss by transpiration

cards.term: What makes up the ground tissue?
cards.definition: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles: parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma

cards.term: Where is parenchyma found in primary stems and roots?
cards.definition: Cortex, pericycle, pith, medullary rays

cards.term: What is mesophyll?
cards.definition: The ground tissue of leaves: thin-walled cells with chloroplasts

cards.term: What makes a vascular bundle?
cards.definition: Xylem and phloem together

cards.term: Open vs closed vascular bundles?
cards.definition: Open: cambium between xylem and phloem, can form secondary tissues (dicot stems). Closed: no cambium (monocots).

cards.term: What is a radial vascular bundle? Where?
cards.definition: Xylem and phloem on alternate radii: in roots

cards.term: What is a conjoint vascular bundle? Where?
cards.definition: Xylem and phloem on the same radius, phloem usually on the outer side: in stems and leaves

cards.term: Name the three types in Figure 6.2.
cards.definition: (a) radial (b) conjoint closed (c) conjoint open (cambium between phloem and xylem)

cards.term: Which dicot root does NCERT section?
cards.definition: Sunflower

cards.term: What is the outermost layer of a root called?
cards.definition: Epiblema (many cells form unicellular root hairs)

cards.term: Describe the root cortex.
cards.definition: Several layers of thin-walled parenchyma with intercellular spaces

cards.term: Describe the root endodermis.
cards.definition: Single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces

cards.term: What are casparian strips?
cards.definition: Deposits of water-impermeable, waxy suberin on the tangential and radial walls of endodermal cells

cards.term: Why do casparian strips matter (intuition)?
cards.definition: They block water from sneaking between cells, forcing it through the cell membranes, so the root controls what enters the xylem

cards.term: What is the pericycle, and what arises from it?
cards.definition: A few layers of thick-walled parenchyma next to the endodermis; lateral roots and vascular cambium (secondary growth) start here

cards.term: What is conjunctive tissue?
cards.definition: Parenchyma between the xylem and phloem in roots

cards.term: How many xylem patches in a dicot root?
cards.definition: Usually two to four (diarch to tetrarch)

cards.term: What is the stele?
cards.definition: All tissues inside the endodermis: pericycle, vascular bundles and pith

cards.term: Is the protoxylem of roots endarch or exarch? (beyond NCERT)
cards.definition: Exarch: protoxylem towards the outside, metaxylem towards the centre. Stems are endarch.

cards.term: Figure 6.3 (a) · T.S. of dicot root (primary)
How many xylem bundles in a monocot root?
cards.definition: Usually more than six (polyarch)

cards.term: Pith: dicot root vs monocot root?
cards.definition: Dicot: small or inconspicuous. Monocot: large and well developed.

cards.term: Do monocot roots show secondary growth?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: T.S. of monocot root: point out what differs from the dicot root.
cards.definition: Polyarch xylem, large pith, no cambium

cards.term: Name the three sub-zones of the cortex in a dicot stem.
cards.definition: Hypodermis, cortical layers, endodermis

cards.term: What is the hypodermis of a dicot stem made of, and what does it do?
cards.definition: A few layers of collenchyma below the epidermis; mechanical strength to the young stem

cards.term: Why is the stem endodermis called the starch sheath?
cards.definition: Its cells are rich in starch grains

cards.term: What is the pericycle like in a dicot stem?
cards.definition: Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma inside the endodermis, above the phloem

cards.term: What are medullary rays?
cards.definition: Radially placed parenchyma between the vascular bundles

cards.term: What is characteristic about vascular bundles in a dicot stem?
cards.definition: Arranged in a ring; each conjoint, open, with endarch protoxylem

cards.term: T.S. of dicot stem: read the labelled figure from outside in.
cards.definition: Epidermis → hypodermis (collenchyma) → cortex (parenchyma) → endodermis → pericycle → vascular bundles in a ring (phloem, cambium, xylem) → pith

cards.term: Hypodermis of a monocot stem?
cards.definition: Sclerenchymatous

cards.term: Vascular bundles of a monocot stem?
cards.definition: Scattered, each with a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath; conjoint and closed

cards.term: Peripheral vs central bundles in a monocot stem?
cards.definition: Peripheral bundles are smaller than central ones

cards.term: Which tissue is absent in monocot stem bundles, and what is present instead?
cards.definition: Phloem parenchyma is absent; water-containing cavities are present

cards.term: A T.S. shows conjoint, scattered bundles with sclerenchymatous sheaths and no phloem parenchyma. What is it?
cards.definition: A monocot stem

cards.term: Dicot vs monocot stem
cards.definition: Hypodermis: Collenchyma (sclerenchyma); Vascular bundles: Ring (scattered); Bundle type: Conjoint, open (conjoint, closed); Ground tissue: Cortex, pith, medullary rays (large undifferentiated)

cards.term: What are the three main parts in a section of a dorsiventral leaf?
cards.definition: Epidermis, mesophyll, vascular system

cards.term: Adaxial vs abaxial epidermis?
cards.definition: Adaxial: upper surface. Abaxial: lower surface.

cards.term: Which leaf surface has more stomata in a dicot leaf?
cards.definition: The abaxial (lower); the adaxial may even lack them

cards.term: Palisade vs spongy parenchyma?
cards.definition: Palisade: adaxial, elongated cells, vertical and parallel. Spongy: below it, oval or round, loosely arranged with large air spaces.

cards.term: What surrounds the vascular bundles of a leaf?
cards.definition: A layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells

cards.term: In a leaf vascular bundle, which side is xylem on?
cards.definition: Adaxial (upper) side, phloem towards the abaxial side

cards.term: How does an isobilateral leaf differ from a dorsiventral one?
cards.definition: Stomata on both surfaces; mesophyll not differentiated into palisade and spongy

cards.term: What are bulliform cells? Where?
cards.definition: Large, empty, colourless adaxial epidermal cells along the veins, in grasses

cards.term: What do bulliform cells do?
cards.definition: Turgid: leaf surface exposed. Flaccid in water stress: leaves curl inwards to reduce water loss.

cards.term: Why are the vascular bundles of a monocot leaf nearly the same size?
cards.definition: Its parallel venation (except main veins)

cards.term: Dicot vs monocot leaf
cards.definition: Stomata: Mostly lower surface (both surfaces); Mesophyll: Palisade + spongy (undifferentiated); Bulliform cells: Absent (present in grasses); Bundles: Vary in size (near similar)

cards.term: Dicot vs monocot root
cards.definition: Xylem bundles: 2–4 (more than 6, polyarch); Pith: Small (large); Secondary growth: Occurs (absent)

cards.term: Name the three kinds of meristem.
cards.definition: Apical, lateral, intercalary
